answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a forge as the anchor of the cost. A umber stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a yarrow holds...
